He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]] and the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. ==High school career== McCullar played basketball for [[Karen Wagner High School]] in [[San Antonio|San Antonio, Texas]]. As a sophomore, he helped his team reach the Class 6A state title game. In his junior season, McCullar averaged 16.8 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, before fracturing his [[tibia]] during the playoffs.{{cite web |last1=Silva Jr. |first1=Carlos |title=McCullar pledges to play for Texas Tech |url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2018/07/06/san-antonio-wagner-guard-mccullar-pledges-to-play-for-texas-tech/11589166007/ |website=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 5, 2018}} He opted to graduate early and bypass his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=Wagner standout McCullar to skip senior season |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/Wagner-standout-McCullar-to-skip-senior-season-12902434.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=May 9, 2018}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] over offers from [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].{{cite web |last1=Hinojosa |first1=David |title=Wagner's McCullar commits to Texas Tech |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high_school/high_school_boys_basketball/article/Wagner-s-McCullar-commits-to-Texas-Tech-13052806.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 5, 2018}} ==College career== McCullar [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season at Texas Tech to rehabilitate after fracturing his tibia as a junior in high school. Despite his absence, his team reached the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship game]].{{cite web |last1=Strader |first1=Jay |title=McCullar finds role for Red Raiders |url=http://www.dailytoreador.com/sports/mccullar-finds-role-for-red-raiders/article_5bfa2ea8-53a2-11ea-b787-9b36b860d0b8.html |website=[[The Daily Toreador]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=February 19, 2020}} As a freshman, McCullar averaged six points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Mainville |first1=Ryan |title=McCullar feeling prepared for new season |url=http://www.dailytoreador.com/sports/mccullar-feeling-prepared-for-new-season/article_ea158530-198a-11eb-9ff5-eb337ed3d258.html |website=[[The Daily Toreador]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=October 28, 2020}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 10.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game, earning All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Marquez |first1=RJ |title=Former SA Wagner standout, Texas Tech star Kevin McCullar Jr. using new NIL laws to build brand, give back to community |url=https://www.ksat.com/news/local/2021/07/19/former-sa-wagner-standout-texas-tech-star-kevin-mccullar-jr-using-new-nil-laws-to-build-brand-give-back-to-community/ |publisher=[[KSAT-TV]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 19, 2021}} On November 12, 2021, he scored a career-high 24 points in an 88–62 win against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]].{{cite news |title=Texas Tech overwhelms Grambling in second half, wins 88–62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372314 |access-date=December 23, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2021}} As a junior, McCullar averaged 10.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game. He hit 28 of 90 three pointers for 31.1%.{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Former Texas Tech Red Raider Kevin McCullar exits NBA Draft, will play for KU Jayhawks |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article262009540.html |work=[[Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=June 2, 2022}} On April 27, 2022, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] while also declaring for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Silva Jr. |first1=Carlos |title=Texas Tech basketball player Kevin McCullar enters name into the NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/04/27/texas-tech-basketball-player-kevin-mccullar-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/9557268002/ |website=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]] |access-date=May 19, 2022 |date=April 27, 2022}} On May 19, 2022, McCullar announced he was transferring to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] while also remaining in the NBA draft.{{Cite web |title=Texas Tech’s Kevin McCullar Announces Decision to Transfer to Kansas |url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/05/20/texas-tech-kevin-mccullar-announces-transfer-kansas-nba-draft|first=Madison|last= Williams|date=May 19, 2022|access-date=May 19, 2022|website=Sports Illustrated}} On June 1, 2022, McCullar removed himself from the NBA Draft and announced he would be playing for the Jayhawks.{{cite news |last=Guskey |first=Jordan |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Kevin McCullar announces he’s exiting NBA draft process, returning to college at Kansas |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/hawk-zone/2022/06/01/kevin-mccullar-texas-tech-nba-draft-2022-ku-kansas-basketball/7470835001/ |work=[[Topeka Capital-Journal]] |location=[[Topeka, Kansas]] |access-date=June 2, 2022}} As a senior, he was named to the Third Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] as well as the All-Defensive Team.{{cite web |title=🏀 Jayhawk Starters Headline 2023 All-Big 12 Honors for Kansas |url=https://kuathletics.com/jayhawk-starters-headline-2023-all-big-12-honors-for-kansas/ |website=[[Kansas Jayhawks]] |access-date=March 6, 2023 |date=March 5, 2023}}
